thread.title_full: Vikings' Injured Rookie Seems Pretty Healthy to Start Camp - NewsBreak

author: Ted Schwerzler
title: Vikings' Injured Rookie Seems Pretty Healthy to Start Camp - NewsBreak
text:
By Ted Schwerzler ,
3 hours ago
When the Minnesota Vikings selected Caleb Banks in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft, they drew heat . The former Florida Gators defensive tackle played just three games during his senior season after injuring his left foot in fall camp and aggravating it against LSU in September. He underwent surgery after that game, then fractured the same foot again while preparing for the NFL Combine .
When healthy, Banks has the potential to become the kind of difference-maker Minnesota hasn’t had on the interior since Kevin and Pat Williams formed the Williams Wall. The first step toward becoming that type of player is staying on the field.
It’s certainly encouraging, then, that Banks began his first NFL training camp on the field. As former Vikings head coach Mike Zimmer used to say, “You can’t make the club in the tub.” The rookie isn’t fighting for a roster spot, but every rep matters after he missed nearly all of last season.
Caleb Banks gets to work for Minnesota Vikings Banks was expected to be ready before the regular season, but how much he could do during training camp remained a question. He answered at least part of that Wednesday by taking an active role in team drills.
His last game action came on Nov. 29, 2025 . The latest foot injury limited his participation at the NFL Combine and likely played a role in him being available at No. 18. His workload may still be managed, but taking part in team drills on Day 1 suggests the Vikings are comfortable with where his recovery stands.
During the two seasons before his injury-plagued senior campaign, Banks appeared in 12 games both years. He was a disruptive interior defender for Florida, totaling 8.5 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks in those contests. At his best, he can be everything Minnesota hoped it was getting.
MN Vikings iDL finally has a chance to thrive Last season, the Minnesota Vikings signed veterans Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave hoping to revitalize their careers and retool the defensive line. It didn’t work out, and both were sent packing.
This time around, the franchise invested in youth and did so in a big way. By drafting Banks in the first round and Domonique Orange in the third, the Vikings may have found fixtures in the middle for years to come. Those two, alongside emerging standout Jalen Redmond, give Brian Flores an intriguing young trio to work with.
Flores’ defense has largely thrived by generating havoc, but consistent disruption from the interior has been lacking. If the two rookies develop as Minnesota hopes, that could finally change.
